name: Dishon
overview: Dishon was a male Edomite, known as a son of Seir and a chief within the Edomite tribe. His identity is firmly rooted in the genealogical records of Edom, emphasizing his role in the leadership structure of this people. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Dishon appears once in Scripture and is understood to mean 'ibex,' a type of wild goat, though this meaning is uncertain. It is a proper name given in the genealogical context rather than a divine or symbolic title.
familyAndRelationships: Dishon is explicitly identified as the son of Seir, anchoring him within the Edomite lineage. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Dishon's significance lies in his position as a chief in Edom, marking him as a figure of authority among the descendants of Seir. His mention in the genealogies highlights the organization and leadership within the Edomite people, who are often referenced in the broader biblical narrative as neighbors and sometimes adversaries of Israel. Through Dishon, the Bible preserves the historical and tribal structure of Edom.
